title: Introduce credential telemetry and lazy streaming shim across SDKs
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add opt-in credential lifecycle telemetry and a lazy streaming shim to reduce memory for long-lived streaming clients; bump Python/TS/Go package minor versions for compatibility and ergonomics.
description: Context and motivation: We observed multiple customer apps holding large streaming handles open for long periods which caused memory pressure and opaque credential behavior during token rotations. This PR introduces two coordinated changes across SDKs: (1) a lightweight credential telemetry API that emits structured lifecycle events (lease_acquired, lease_renewed, lease_failed, credential_fallback) so platform teams can build alerting and SLOs; (2) a lazy streaming shim / pull-iterator that defers allocation of internal buffers and KV cache warmups until the first read, improving memory footprint for idle streams and making streaming ergonomics simpler for async consumers. Design highlights: unified event names and fields across Python/TS/Go (schema in docs/telemetry.md), opt-in by default for existing callers but enabled in new examples; lazy stream implements __aiter__/__anext__ (Python), AsyncIterable/AsyncIterator (TS), and a lightweight PullStream interface for Go. Backwards compatibility: the shim preserves existing streaming surface and supports feature flags for strict parity mode. Checklist: - [x] API surface proposal reviewed with SDK leads (ENG-5421) - [x] Schema documented in docs/telemetry.md - [x] Unit and integration tests for credential edge cases and stream reattach - [x] Performance bench against previous release across p50/p95 and resident memory - [x] Version bumps in Python/TS/Go packaging Summary of changes and commits: commit 1: add credential telemetry interface and basic emitter; commit 2: implement lazy stream shim in Python SDK and tests; commit 3: mirror shim + telemetry in TypeScript example and update typings; commit 4: add lightweight PullStream adapter in Go and plumbing to the credential mediator; commit 5: update docs and changelogs, bump versions. Files changed (high level): python/pyproject.toml, python/src/redwood/streaming.py, python/src/redwood/credentials/telemetry.py, typescript/package.json, typescript/src/stream/lazyStream.ts, go/sdk/credentials.go, docs/telemetry.md. CI and checks: unit, lint, typecheck passed; integration suite (cross-sdk) ran in a dedicated job and passed after a flaky test (stream-resume) rerun. Performance results: in an internal benchmark that simulates 3k concurrent idle-forwarding handles, resident memory dropped ~8% overall and p50 response latency improved ~12% for first-token in warmed paths due to deferred cache warmup; cold-start first-token latency increased by ~4ms in microbench. Review discussion (high level): Jonah: asked to ensure telemetry event shapes are minimal and stable; requested example of linking lease events to request traces. Maya: replied with section in docs describing trace_id propagation and added a unit that surfaces trace headers. Priya: requested an opt-out env var for enterprises; implemented REDWOOD_SDK_STRICT_STREAMING to force previous allocation strategy. Erik: sign-off on Go ergonomics after minor API rename in credential mediator. Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2026-02-22 (merge_method: squash). Notes and followups: plan a follow-up PR to add end-to-end alerting examples in observability-pack and to wire telemetry into the console ingestion pipeline (ENG-5480).

changelog_entry: Added credential lifecycle telemetry (opt-in), introduced lazy streaming shim to reduce memory for idle streams, bumped SDK minor versions for Python/TS/Go, and added config flag REDWOOD_SDK_STRICT_STREAMING for legacy behavior.
